Survey design and weighting

Source: vignettes/articles/survey-design.Rmd
survey-design.Rmd

Build the cohort design

nis_design() validates YEAR, HOSP_NIS, NIS_STRATUM, and DISCWT, then constructs a survey design before applying the declared domain.

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmpld4uTJ/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).

#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmpld4uTJ/duckdb

#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmpld4uTJ/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
design <- nis_design(
  nis,
  cohort = heart_failure & AGE >= 18,
  keep = c(AGE, LOS),
  annualize = TRUE
)
#> Warning: Missing values are always removed in SQL aggregation functions.
#> Use `na.rm = TRUE` to silence this warning
#> This warning is displayed once every 8 hours.
#> Cohort: 108 discharges; weighted N 62.4; 18 hospitals across 2 years.
srvyr::summarise(design, total = srvyr::survey_total(),
                 mean_los = srvyr::survey_mean(LOS))
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   total total_se mean_los mean_los_se
#>   <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1  62.4     8.67     5.66       0.229

The output contains a weighted fixture total and mean LOS with design-based standard errors. Empty cohort hospital-years are retained as zero-domain placeholder rows so domain variance uses the full sampled structure. This placeholder strategy is experimental.

Choose a pooling convention

Without annualization, pooled-year weights represent the combined included period. annualize = TRUE divides by the number of valid years; partial years count as a year. When quarter fields are present the function warns about incomplete year coverage and a 2015 cohort restricted to one coding era. Exclude partial years or choose a documented alternative if this convention does not fit the estimand.

nis_reweight() multiplies the design weights by analyst-supplied weights. It is experimental and does not replace the NIS discharge weight or the survey design.

weighted <- nis_reweight(design, weights = rep(1, nrow(design$variables)))
srvyr::summarise(weighted, total = srvyr::survey_total())
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   total total_se
#>   <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1  62.4     8.67

With unit multipliers the result retains the original design-weighted total. This is only a syntax example, not a recommended reweighting model.

Why design-based standard errors matter

NIS uses hospital clusters, strata, and discharge weights. Ordinary means and standard errors treat rows as if they came from a simple random sample and do not reflect that structure. Use srvyr or survey methods on the returned design for point estimates and uncertainty. A survey standard error is an estimate of sampling variability under the supplied design, not a guarantee that all sources of bias have been addressed.

Inspect exclusions

Rows with missing, non-finite, or non-positive design fields are excluded before the cohort is applied. Inspect the aggregate audit attribute and report the exclusions with the analysis.

attr(design, "nis_excluded")
#> $total
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $by_field
#>        YEAR    HOSP_NIS NIS_STRATUM      DISCWT 
#>           0           0           0           0 
#> 
#> $by_year
#> # A tibble: 0 × 2
#> # ℹ 2 variables: YEAR <int>, n <dbl>

This list gives counts by field and year, not record-level information.

Common pitfalls

Common pitfalls

  • Filtering the source data to the cohort before constructing the design removes non-cohort sampled records.
  • Treating annualized weights as a correction for arbitrary partial-year coverage.
  • Using non-survey summaries for estimates or uncertainty.
  • Treating reweighting or placeholder-row variance methods as established methods; both are experimental.

See nis_design(), nis_reweight(), and Data notes by year.
